info.name: Armada API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Armada multi-agent orchestration system.

Version: 1.2.0

## Setup
1. Set the `baseUrl` variable to your Admiral server (default: `http://localhost:7890`)
2. For bearer token auth, set `bearerToken` (the default credential token is `default`)
3. For session token auth, use the Authenticate request and set `sessionToken` from the response
4. Legacy: If API key authentication is enabled, set the `apiKey` variable (deprecated)
5. Use the Status > Health Check request to verify connectivity

## Role model
- IsAdmin=true: global system-wide admin
- IsAdmin=false and IsTenantAdmin=true: tenant-scoped admin
- IsAdmin=false and IsTenantAdmin=false: regular user with self-service on own account and credentials

## Data scoping
Armada scopes data per user within a tenant, in two categories.

**Category A - owned operational entities** (fleets, vessels, voyages, captains, missions, docks, signals, events, merge queue, objectives/backlog): a regular user sees/manages only rows they own; a tenant admin sees the whole tenant; a global admin sees everything. Enumeration is scoped from the caller's identity. Admins may narrow the view with the `userId` query filter (and a global admin with `tenantId`) on list/enumerate requests; these filters are ignored when they would exceed a regular user's own scope.

**Category B - shared configuration entities** (model endpoints, playbooks, skills, prompt templates, personas, pipelines, workflow profiles, project profiles, runbooks): each object carries an ownership scope, `TenantWide` or `UserSpecific`, in a `scope` field (workflow profiles and project profiles use `ownershipScope`, because their `scope` field means application scope - Global/Fleet/Vessel). Reads for a regular user return all tenant-wide objects plus their own user-specific objects. A regular user may create only user-specific objects (the requested scope is coerced) and may edit/delete only their own; tenant-wide objects require a tenant admin. Only admins may change an object's ownership scope. Include `"scope": "UserSpecific"` or `"scope": "TenantWide"` in create/update bodies to set it (admins only for TenantWide).

Note: MCP tools run as the MCP caller (credential identity, a mission-scoped token for mission captains, or the default tenant's tenant admin for unauthenticated loopback callers when Mcp.AllowUnauthenticatedLoopback is on), check a declared permission level per tool, and resolve entity ids in the caller's scope like REST.

## Notes
- Tenant, user, and credential protection is server-controlled through IsProtected
- Immutable fields such as IDs, ownership columns, and creation timestamps are preserved server-side on update
- Includes Objectives, Delivery workflow profiles, structured checks, environments, deployments, incidents, runbooks, releases, cross-entity history, Workspace, Planning Sessions, Request History, Mux runtime helpers, and OpenAPI discovery examples.

request.description: Rebuilds the Admiral from source and cuts over to the new build. Publishes the configured Armada source (resolved from SelfVesselId, or an explicit SourcePath) into a fresh versioned slot from a detached git worktree at the requested ref, backs up the database, flips the active-slot pointer, and hands over to the new build. The build runs while the current instance keeps serving; only a successful server publish triggers a cutover. All body fields are optional (Ref blank builds current HEAD). Poll GET /api/v1/server/rebuild/status for progress. Requires global admin when RequireAuthForShutdown is true.

item.name: Black Box
item.description:
Mission and voyage black box entries: where, how and why a mission or voyage failed, with evidence, analysis, ranked recovery paths and briefs for agents, users and maintainers (MISSION_BLACKBOX_PLAN.md). One request per route in src/Armada.Server/Routes/BlackBoxRoutes.cs plus the mission read that carries LastBlackBoxEntryId.

The folder runs top to bottom against any Admiral that has at least one current entry. Find a current black box entry stores blackboxEntryId, missionId, voyageId and blackboxFingerprint; Read the Analysis section stores blackboxPathId (and blackboxRecommendationId when the analysis has one); List entry objects stores blackboxObjectName. The recovery requests run in order: refused without a token (409 BlackBoxConfirmationRequired), dry run (stores the bbc_ token in blackboxConfirmToken), confirmed run. The confirmed run really executes the path (for bbx-exec-006.restart it restarts the mission), so use a throwaway Admiral. Deletes run last and target blackboxDeleteId, a placeholder id by default, so a run does not delete the entry it reads.

Errors use the standard error body with Data.Code: BlackBoxNotFound (404, also for other tenants' entries), BlackBoxDeleting (409), BlackBoxConfirmationRequired (409), InvalidArgument (400), BlackBoxStoreUnavailable (503). See postman/README.md for seeding an entry, running this folder with the Postman CLI, and the example-replay mock in postman/mocks/blackbox.
